confidence: High – We identified over 100 entities from authoritative sources (SEC filings and company records). The list covers Citigroup’s most significant and many minor subsidiaries across regions. Given the extensive sources and cross-verification, confidence is high that this is a comprehensive representation of Citigroup’s active legal entities. However, Citigroup’s total legal entities count (around 5,900+ globally) suggests there may be numerous very small or special-purpose entities not individually listed here because they are not material to financial statements.
research_notes:
Primary research revolved around SEC filings (especially Exhibit 21 in annual 10-K reports) which provided a baseline list of major subsidiaries ([www.sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000083100115000043/citi-exhibit2101x12312014.htm#:~:text=Following%20is%20a%20list%20of,as%20of%20December%2031%2C%202014)). By reviewing multiple years (2014, 2019, 2023 filings), we captured both current significant subsidiaries and additional entities that appeared in prior lists (indicating historical or smaller units). The SEC Exhibit 21 for 2014 was particularly valuable as it listed many subsidiaries (including smaller finance and leasing companies) omitted in later filings ([www.sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000083100115000043/citi-exhibit2101x12312014.htm#:~:text=Citigroup%20Fund%20Services%20Canada%2C%20Inc,Delaware)). We augmented this with international and official sources: for example, Citigroup’s own “Global Presence” pages (like Citi Canada) confirmed specific local subsidiaries (e.g., Canadian and U.K. entities) ([www.citigroup.com](https://www.citigroup.com/global/about-us/global-presence/canada?ieNocache=47#:~:text=Citibank%20Canada%2C%20Citibank%2C%20N,are%20subsidiaries)). We also cross-checked select jurisdictions via corporate registries and LEI databases (such as UK Companies House for Citibank UK Ltd. and LEI records for certain entities) to verify existence and jurisdiction. 
Gaps and limitations: While our list is extensive, it may not include every minor or dormant entity, as Citigroup’s corporate structure is extremely large and fluid. Very small or recently formed entities that are not publicly disclosed (due to immateriality) could be missing. We focused on wholly-owned and majority-owned entities; significant joint ventures (if any) have been included if publicly known. The list appears complete for all major operating companies and regional holdings, and includes many smaller subsidiaries across different business lines and countries. However, it is still a partial aggregation relative to the ~5,900 legal entities Citigroup reportedly maintains worldwide. 
The research was challenging due to Citigroup’s global span – requiring over 25 distinct search queries and source checks. Changes over time (sales of operations in certain countries, name changes like Citigroup Finance Canada Inc. becoming ULC, etc.) required comparing historical filings and news. We noted, for instance, entities related to Citi’s consumer finance arm (CitiFinancial/OneMain) were present in older filings ([www.sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/831001/000083100115000043/citi-exhibit2101x12312014.htm#:~:text=CitiFinancial%20Services%2C%20Inc.%26lt%3BMN%26gt%3B%20%20,Texas)) but have since been sold and thus are excluded as current subsidiaries. We have either omitted or noted such cases. 
Overall, this list is as complete as public information allows – covering Citi’s key banking entities (Citibank N.A. and its overseas banks), securities broker-dealers (Citigroup Global Markets entities in various countries), holding companies and service companies. Further research could involve using specialized corporate hierarchy databases or contacting Citigroup’s investor relations for an official full list, but the above should encompass all significant and many minor Citigroup affiliates. Any future acquisitions, disposals, or internal restructurings could change the roster, so a periodic review of SEC filings and international registry updates is recommended to maintain an up-to-date list.
